title: An ancient Chinese irrigation system splits a river without a dam
body: In the third century BCE, Li Bing began work on Dujiangyan in what is now Sichuan. Channels and a diversion embankment split the flow so some water could reach fields while the river continued downstream.
takeaway: Diverting part of a flow can supply a plain without stopping the whole river at a wall.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Dujiangyan Irrigation System Nomination
visual: a river branching around a tapered stone embankment at Dujiangyan

title: Sado Island preserves different ways to mine gold without machinery
body: On Japan's Sado Island, miners worked loose deposits at Nishimikawa and solid veins in rock in the Aikawa-Tsurushi area. The two landscapes preserve traces of different techniques used before mechanised extraction.
takeaway: The form in which ore occurs changes the tools and the layout of the works needed to reach it.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Sado Island Gold Mines (2024)
visual: a narrow old mine entrance in wooded volcanic rock on Sado Island
